correctness.rationale: The energy generator equations follow from the uniform split and the independent exponential refresh. For existence, the fixed-block affine update has linear part of l1 norm at most one, strictly below one on a positive-probability refresh–exchange–refresh sequence. Its additive term is bounded in l1 by a finite-block compound-Poisson sum with every finite moment. The backward affine series thus converges in Lp for fixed p by independence of blocks and summable geometric Lp bounds on the linear products. The same block contraction gives uniqueness, and invariance under the full semigroup follows from uniqueness for the block chain. For an independent moment derivation, use the product-exponential mixture: the edge product Laplace transform for means a,b equals the integral of (1+s(ua+(1−u)b))^−2 over uniform u, and uniform re-splitting of that conditional gamma sum gives two independent exponentials with the common new mean. Let q=1+2r and center hidden temperatures at T in units of Δ for Δ≠0. Their hub mean is zero and leaf means are σ_i A for A=2r/q. Balanced sign reflection makes their hub-square Z, common leaf-square L and hub–leaf product H label-symmetric. Edge averaging gives 2Z=L+H and the leaf refresh gives L=(Z+r)/(1+r). For i≠j the leaf product is H/q+A²σ_iσ_j; hence the hub–leaf equation gives Z=[1+r+(N−1)r/q]H+A²/2. These solve to H=1/[q(N+q)], Z=r/q+(r+1)/[q²(N+q)] and L=A+1/[q²(N+q)]. This derivation is valid at N=2 as well. Distinct energy covariances equal hidden covariances and each energy variance is its mean squared plus twice its hidden variance. This gives every displayed moment and the fixed-r limit. At Δ=0 the independent product exponentials are invariant. The frozen scripts were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The star is a natural high-degree non-equilibrium network with both like-bath and opposite-bath pairs. The exact identity shows their covariances coincide despite unequal stationary means; those covariances disappear with degree while the hub retains a nonthermal variance. This distinguishes decorrelation from convergence of local statistics to equilibrium and supplies an explicit benchmark for finite-rate exchange, without claiming a full limiting distribution.
